name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Push link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day (the access gate)

name: Reel
text: We should assign a dedicated team member to review and update the link coverage daily, ensuring we meet the +5%/day target. This decision is best because it allows for consistent progress and prompt identification of gaps in coverage, enabling us to adjust our strategy as needed. By doing this, we're accepting the trade-off of dedicating a team member's time and resources to this task, potentially diverting attention from other important tasks. This focus, however, is necessary to push link coverage toward 100% effectively.

name: Scriv
text: Assigning a dedicated reviewer won’t fix the core problem: if the team lacks the authority to enforce link fixes, the reviewer becomes a bottleneck, not a solution. Instead, tie link coverage to the pull request gate—block merges until coverage meets the threshold. That settles it: either the PRs get fixed, or the work stalls, forcing ownership.

name: Chisel
text:
We should tie link coverage to the pull request gate, automatically blocking merges until coverage meets the threshold. This decision is best because it ensures that link fixes are addressed promptly and consistently, without relying on a dedicated reviewer or adding unnecessary bureaucracy. By doing this, we accept the trade-off of potentially slower development cycles if coverage thresholds are not met, but this is outweighed by the benefit of guaranteed progress toward our 100% link coverage goal. This approach also distributes the responsibility for link coverage across the team, rather than placing it on a single reviewer.

name: Sift
text: The real risk is that tying link coverage to the pull request gate could lead to teams prioritizing short-term fixes over meaningful improvements, just to meet the threshold. A better alternative might be to introduce a secondary review process that verifies the quality of link fixes, rather than just their presence. This would settle the argument: either we prioritize thorough, high-quality link coverage or we risk gaming the system with superficial fixes.
